# Proper nouns that may be capitalized inside a heading.
#
# This is the single source of truth for the heading-case rules. Two rule files
# are generated from it; do not edit the generated parts by hand:
#
#   vale/styles/ROCm/CORE-008.yml     (reStructuredText) - each line becomes
#                                      one `exceptions:` entry
#   vale/styles/ROCm/CORE-008-MD.yml  (Markdown)         - each line is split
#                                      into words, and the plain Capitalized
#                                      words become part of one regex
#
# After editing this file run:
#
#   python scripts/sync-heading-exceptions.py
#
# CI runs the same script with --check and fails if the rule files are stale.
#
# Format: one name per line. Blank lines and lines starting with "#" are
# ignored. Write names as plain text; regex special characters are escaped by
# the script.
#
# What belongs here, and what does not:
#   - Add a proper noun that is a plain Capitalized Word, or a multi-word name
#     containing one ("Docker", "Strix Halo", "Visual Studio Code").
#   - Do NOT add acronyms, camelCase names, or model numbers ("GPU", "XGBoost",
#     "MI300X"). Any word with two or more capitals is already exempt in both
#     rules, so listing it is harmless but redundant.
#   - Do NOT add ordinary section words ("Notes", "Guidelines", "Support").
#     Those are the genuine Title Case violations the rule exists to catch.
#
# How a multi-word name is matched:
#   - Markdown: each plain Capitalized word is exempt only where it sits inside
#     the listed name. Listing "GitHub Issues" exempts "Issues" after "GitHub",
#     but "Resolved Issues" is still flagged.
#   - reStructuredText: the whole phrase is exempt, and nothing else.
#
# A name may end with " @md" to apply to Markdown only. Use it when the
# reStructuredText rule mishandles a phrase that starts with a word containing
# two or more capitals ("ROCr Runtime", "GitHub Issues"): Vale lets its
# hand-written multi-capital pattern consume the first word, leaving the second
# exposed. After adding such a name, check it as a whole reStructuredText
# heading; see vale/testdata/core-008-rst-acronyms.rst.
